title: Thomas Edison
summary: American inventor, born in Milan, Ohio, on 11 February 1847. In 1876 he left Newark for Menlo Park, New Jersey, where his laboratory produced the tin foil phonograph (1877) and a practical electric lighting system first shown publicly in December 1879. He later built a larger laboratory at West Orange, New Jersey, and by his death on 18 October 1931 held 1,093 US patents.

uncertainty.note: Day-level birth and death dates given by the National Park Service; Rutgers confirms the year and day of death.

as_recorded.value: In 1876 Edison sold all his Newark manufacturing concerns

importance.justification: Prolific American inventor and founder of an industrial research laboratory; his phonograph and lighting system shaped the electric age.
